route: No independent-means route. Island.is lists permits for work, students, spouses, children, au pair, parents (over 67 and financially dependent), permanent residence and 'special ties', which is granted 'only in exceptional cases' where family ties and past stays weigh most. For any permit: 'An insurance certificate must be submitted, confirming that the applicant has taken out (purchased) a health insurance that is valid in Iceland, for at least three months from the date of the registration of the applicant's legal domicile in Iceland, with a minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000.' Means of support for special ties: 415,922 ISK a month for a married couple.
policy: Three-month bridge policy from an Icelandic insurer (Sjóvá, TM, VIS, Vordur) with ISK 2,000,000 insured sum; Sjóvá deductible ISK 50,000, pre-existing conditions and pregnancy excluded, valid in Iceland only. After three months from registered domicile (rule from 1 August 2026, was six months) the couple are in Icelandic Health Insurance (Sjukratryggingar), tax-funded with patient fees. No individual premium was found.
working: No premium: Sjóvá, TM and VIS show no price (quote is by application; Sjóvá says the premium is 'the minimum premium for a period of up to three months' and 'depends on the age'). Public cover: no premium found, so 0 apart from patient fees. work.iceland.is gives a general patient payment ceiling of 37,794 ISK (per person, and that page still says six months so may be out of date). Amount left null because the bridge cost is unknown.

eu_citizen_difference: EEA and Nordic citizens moving from another EEA state can transfer cover without the waiting period and need no residence permit for the first three months.
spot_check: None possible: no insurer publishes the premium. Sjóvá, TM and VIS terms agree on the three-month bridge and ISK 2,000,000.
uncertainty: Bridge premium unknown (probably small, a one-off for three months, but not sourced). Iceland has no independent-means route, so the couple would only arrive by another route (for example family). Public patient-fee ceiling is from a stale page. An 'sjukratryggingagjald' charged to individuals was not found; I did not check the Icelandic tax pages.
